claims.nodeLabel: Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263) - AARO establishment, Historical Record Report and annual reports
claims.sourceText: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-117publ263/html/PLAW-117publ263.htm ; phrase quoted is AARO's, from HRR Volume I pp. 6 and 45 — https://media.defense.gov/2024/Mar/08/2003409233/-1/-1/0/DOPSR-2024-0263-AARO-HISTORICAL-RECORD-REPORT-VOLUME-1-2024.PDF
claims.text: The statute requires ONE Historical Record Report, not a series. The division into 'Volume I' and 'Volume II' is AARO's own construction, and AARO tied Volume II to 'the date established in Section 6802' - which is the same 540-day date, 15 June 2024. On the statute's own terms the Historical Record Report requirement has been only partially discharged since 15 June 2024. Reasoning: Sec. 6802(j)(1)(A) text compared against HRR Vol I pp. 6 and 45.

edges.note: The AARO Historical Record Report Volume I (March 2024) and the FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report contain no discussion of misappropriated funds, illegal contracting, IR&D or contractor financial arrangements. The absence is attested by the reports themselves.

b.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)

edges.label: Irreconcilable executive-branch findings on the same allegations
edges.note: The ICIG found the complaint credible and urgent in July 2022; AARO found no verifiable information from June 2023 and no firsthand knowledge in March 2024. Both are executive-branch determinations on the same body of allegations, and neither has been formally reconciled on the public record. Reasoning: no document exists in which either office addresses the other's finding.

b.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

edges.label: IC-side SAP control office enterprise under DNI authority
edges.note: AARO names three distinct SAP control office enterprises - DoD, IC and DHS. The IC enterprise operates under the DNI's compartmentation authority and is not reported under 10 U.S.C. 119 to the defense committees.

a.label: Intelligence Community special access program control office enterprise

b.label: Program structure and organisational mapping

edges.label: the parallel control-office enterprise on the intelligence-community side of the same architecture
edges.note: The IC maintains its own special access and controlled access program control architecture under DNI authority, separate from the DoD SAP enterprise administered by DoD SAPCO. AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I confirms its existence in the government's own UAP record. The two-sided structure matters because a programme can be lodged on either side, and the oversight statutes differ.

edges.note: The 10 November 1980 AFOSI record documents Kirtland security police observations of unexplained objects over Coyote Canyon and notes Bennewitz's photography and reporting.

edges.label: AARO's 2024 historical review does not mention Rendlesham
edges.note: A congressionally directed review of the historical record omits the best-documented physical-trace incident at a NATO nuclear-capable base, for which the Pentagon's own FOIA office has released the commander's memorandum.

b.label: Paul Frederick Bennewitz

edges.label: Two-sided: the reported admission, and his own recorded denial of harm
edges.note: The board already carries the admission side, reported by Alejandro Rojas on 13 May 2014 in a piece that paraphrases throughout and quotes him nowhere. This edge adds the half that was missing: on camera to George Knapp he calls the harm narrative false 'in every aspect' and says Bennewitz 'did this to himself'. Both are his. Neither can be graded above Tier 2 and the board should carry both rather than choosing.

edges.note: The Deseret News reported the sale in June 1996 and Bigelow confirmed in August 1998 that the Shermans had agreed as a condition of purchase to keep quiet about what they had witnessed.

edges.label: directed the production of the official history
edges.note: The Volume I historical review was drafted under Kirkpatrick's directorship of AARO and released in early 2024 after his departure; he has publicly identified himself with its findings.

b.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)

edges.label: AARO Director's programmatic access ran through the SAPCO enterprise
edges.note: Kirkpatrick directed AARO throughout the period covered by the Historical Record Report, so the 'full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs' assurance is his. Reasoning: the report is AARO's product under his directorship, and no independent verification of the SAP list handed to AARO has been produced.

b.label: Immaculate Constellation 12-page report entered into the Congressional Record

edges.label: Former AARO director denied the programme's existence
edges.note: Kirkpatrick, who authored Volume I's methodology, publicly denied that Immaculate Constellation exists.

a.label: Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263) - AARO establishment, Historical Record Report and annual reports

b.label: Enacted Statute

edges.label: rewrote 50 U.S.C. 3373 to establish AARO and to mandate the Historical Record Report
edges.note: Sec. 6802 of P.L. 117-263, enacted 23 December 2022, added subsection (j) requiring a Historical Record Report within 540 days and subsection (k) requiring joint DNI/SECDEF annual reports. This is the authority AARO itself cites for both report series, which makes it enacted law with directly observable output.

b.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I

edges.label: AARO's 2024 review does not mention the Wilson-Davis notes or Admiral Wilson
edges.note: The most specific custody allegation in the modern record, whose author and subject are both alive and identifiable, is absent from the government's historical review.

b.label: David Charles Grusch

edges.label: The 2002 notes and the 2023 sworn testimony describe the same access-denial mechanism
edges.note: Both describe an appropriately cleared official being refused a read-on by programme security officers and contractor gatekeepers on need-to-know grounds. Twenty-one years apart, two officials describe the same wall.

b.label: Robertson Panel

edges.label: third iteration of the external-scientific-panel pattern after Robertson (1953) and Condon (1966-68)
edges.note: Each prior panel supplied an authoritative dismissal on terms set by the sponsoring agency. Whether this one differs depends on its access to the Governance Board's classified holdings, which has not been publicly described.

b.label: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (UT-Battelle, LLC)

edges.label: DOE laboratory performed AARO's metallic specimen analysis
edges.note: AARO's published materials analysis synopsis was produced with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, a DOE laboratory - meaning DOE analytical capability was the government's chosen instrument for testing alleged recovered material.
